description: Amends Aspen Ridge plan, removing eastern land and buffer.
Adds multi-unit and residential care home sites; rezones FUD.
Neighborhood area decreases; population slightly increases.

chips.text: Approved
Superintendent Martin confirmed schools can accommodate population increase.
Aspen Ridge neighborhood residents affected by plan changes.
Two individuals provided feedback, one raising traffic and parking concerns.
Linear park construction, Link Later, slated to start this year.

description: Redesignates 702 and 706 Victoria Avenue to high-density residential.
Rezones 702 and 706 Victoria Avenue from RM3 to RM5.
Permits a six-story multi-unit building via a zoning agreement.

chips.text: Approved
353 property owners near 702 and 706 Victoria Avenue were notified.
Concerns raised about local traffic, rear lane use, and construction impacts.
Shadow studies showed no significant difference between 15m and 26m building heights.
Developer committed to providing more on-site parking stalls than units in the building.

speakers.name: James Peirce
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: 702 and 706 Victoria Ave
said: Proposes a 6-story, 23-meter condominium building for a prominent site.
Argues height increase has minimal shadow impact, fits area context.
Design features active street frontage, green roof, and ample parking.

segments.title: Administration presents proposed development
description: Six-story multi-unit dwelling proposed at Victoria and 11th.
Requires OCP amendment to high-density residential.
Requires rezoning to RN5 with a zoning agreement.
Proposal aligns with policies due to site characteristics.

chips.text: Residents near 702 and 706 Victoria Avenue
Zoning agreement used to cap building at six stories

segments.title: Questions for administration
description: Heritage impact statement for adjacent residence accepted.
Underground excavation not extending to rear lane.
Zoning agreement does not set minimum parking rates.
Parking decision left to developer due to transit access.

chips.text: Administration explains why parking minimums are not set

segments.title: Developer presents building design and project rationale
description: Six-story residential condominium building proposed.
Seeks amendment for height up to 26 meters (building 23 meters).
Will have 33 to 37 units, depending on sales.
Shadow studies show minimal difference from current allowance.

chips.text: Future residents seeking bespoke condominium living

segments.title: Questions for developer
description: More than 39 parking stalls planned, exceeding unit count.
Flexible unit numbers (33-37) will not affect exterior.
Developer understands heritage sensitivity of the area.
Building targets underserved market for diverse housing.

chips.text: Developer states customers want parking, influencing design
Developer emphasizes building a 'bespoke' product for the city

segments.title: Short-term rentals and zoning agreement
description: Condo board cannot prevent property rentals in province.
Short-term rentals can be included in zoning agreement.
Developer does not expect building to be target for Airbnb.
Such uses require specific inclusion in the agreement.

chips.text: Province's law prevents preventing rentals
Short-term rentals would need explicit inclusion in zoning agreement

segments.title: Zoning by agreement process and tradeoffs
description: Zoning agreement controls specific development on single site.
Used to cap height at six stories, not RN5 maximum.
Provides custom regulations for developer's design aspects.
Allows variances for setbacks and balconies.

chips.text: Agreement provides flexibility for site-specific design features
Agreement sets a specific height limit below the zone's maximum

segments.title: Construction techniques and traffic impacts
description: Excavation will migrate from lane to mitigate ground disturbance.
Ground is stable, no vibration or disturbance expected.
Access plan being worked on for 11th Street.
Alternative routes available for 11th Street residents.

chips.text: Residents on 11th Street regarding traffic and access

segments.title: Motion to approve OCP amendment and rezoning
description: Motion made to approve the applications.
Motion carried by council.

chips.text: Official Community Plan amendment and rezoning approved

description: Permits two garden/garage suites per two-unit dwelling, up to four units.
Removes two-story height limits for garden/garage suites with rear lanes.
Allows six units on corner lots in Transit Development Area as discretionary.

chips.text: Approved
Administration explained six units as discretionary allows council review of changing development.
Developers and residents near corner lots in Transit Development Area are affected.
Public comments raised concerns about traffic, parking, and servicing impacts.
